description: The bar chart titled “Factual Errors” compares the number of factual errors across four question-answering datasets — HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC — under three different QA methods: NoR QA (orange with grid pattern), OneR QA (red with dot pattern), and IRCOT QA (blue with diagonal stripe pattern). The vertical y-axis represents the count of factual errors, ranging from 0 to 40 in increments of 5. For HotpotQA, NoR QA has 15 errors, OneR QA has 10, and IRCOT QA has 5 (though the bar is faintly visible and labeled as 5 in the original chart, it appears as a small gray bar in this image). For 2WikiMQA, NoR QA has 29 errors, OneR QA has 23, and IRCOT QA has 14. For MuSiQue, NoR QA has 28, OneR QA has 27, and IRCOT QA has 23. For IIRC, NoR QA has 15, OneR QA has 14, and IRCOT QA has 11. The chart visually demonstrates that IRCOT QA consistently produces fewer factual errors than the other two methods across all datasets, with the most significant reduction observed in 2WikiMQA and HotpotQA. The bars are grouped by dataset along the horizontal x-axis, and each group contains three bars corresponding to the three QA methods, with values explicitly labeled atop each bar.
